notes: Tie: Photons to Photos' hub lens-construction-data table (.local/lens-normal/modeldata.tsv, row "JP2015-215560	Example01P		Nikon AF-S Nikkor 500mm f/4E FL ED VR") ties this patent's Example 1 to the Nikon AF-S NIKKOR 500mm f/4E FL ED VR (announced 7/2/2015, https://www.nikon.com/company/news/2015/0702_lens_01/). A second row in the same file ties the SAME patent number's Example02P to a different, older lens (AF-S 500mm f/4D IF-ED II) -- that mapping is almost certainly a data-entry slip in the hub table (JP2015-215560 has only 3 examples in the patent itself, at f=490/392/588mm, none obviously an 'Example 2' match for a 1996-era AF-D lens); not used here, and not investigated further since Example 1 is the one this task needs.

Independent corroboration of the tie (not just trusting the hub table): elements/groups counted from Example 1's own cementing pattern (front FLG excluded as a plate) are 16 elements in 12 groups, EXACTLY matching Nikon's published 'Lens Construction: 16 elements in 12 groups' for this product (https://www.nikonusa.com/p/af-s-nikkor-500mm-f4e-fl-ed-vr/20053/overview). Two elements (L11, L12) share nd=1.43385/vd=95.25, the dispersion of a fluorite-class (CaF2) glass, matching Nikon's marketed '2 fluorite elements' (source: Nikon 7/2/2015 press release, and the '500mm f/4E FL' name itself, FL = fluorite). This element/group match is a strong, independent check beyond the hub table's own identification.

Open item, ED-glass count: Nikon markets this lens with 2 ED elements, but THREE elements in this patent example share the same nd=1.49782/vd=82.57 (surfaces 10, 19 and 24 -- L15, L32 and L35, each the rear/cemented element of a different doublet). The patent gives no glass names, only nd/vd/theta_gf, so which two (if any) of these three correspond to Nikon's marketed 'ED' elements cannot be determined from the patent text alone; recorded as an open question rather than guessed.

Elements/groups counted the same way as p500.json: the front protective filter glass (surfaces 1-2, plate: "filter") is a plane-parallel element with no optical power and is excluded from both the elements and groups counts, matching how Nikon's own spec (16/12) evidently also excludes it (16 power elements: L11,L12,L13,L14,L15,L21,L22,L23,L31,L32,L33,L34,L35,L36,L37,L38; 12 groups by cementing: G1 = L11 | L12 | L13 | (L14+L15) = 4 groups; G2 = L21 | (L22+L23) = 2 groups; G3a = (L31+L32) = 1 group; G3b = L33 | (L34+L35) = 2 groups; G3c = L36 | L37 | L38 = 3 groups; total 4+2+1+2+3 = 12).
No aspheric surfaces are printed in Example 1's table (checked the patent text for an aspheric-coefficient section; none present for this example), consistent with an all-spherical telephoto design.

Focus: patent explicitly labels this an inner-focus design, G2 moving toward the image side for near focus (text: '第2レンズ群G2を光軸に沿って像側へ移動させることにより、無限遠物体から近距離物体への合焦を行う'), with the aperture stop fixed. Two variable air gaps are printed, d11 (surface 11, G1-to-G2 gap; this file's surface index 10) and d16 (surface 16, G2-to-stop gap; this file's surface index 15), at three focus states (infinity / intermediate / close). No VariableGap entries are recorded in `focus.gaps` because the patent's close-focus row gives only a magnification (β = -0.153 at close, -0.033 at intermediate), not an object distance in mm, and computing an equivalent object distance from β would require re-deriving the close-focus system's principal-plane shift (the whole prescription's spacings change between focus states) -- doable in principle but not attempted here to avoid a number that looks patent-stated but is actually a multi-step derivation; the raw d11/d16 values themselves are recorded verbatim in each gap surface's own label instead.

Image stabilization: the patent's G3b (this file's L33, L34, L35, surfaces 20-24 / indices 19-23) is the shift (VR) group, moving perpendicular to the optical axis for stabilization; not a focus group. Not modeled as a VariableGap since it does not change t values, only lateral position.

Every semi-diameter is sdSource='estimated-from-marginal-ray', run via .local/n500fl/paraxial.py (a copy of .local/lens-tele/paraxial.py, same method: marginal ray sized from the stated Fno at surface 1, plus a paraxial chief ray at the stated half field 2ω/2 = 2.5175°, summed) -- the patent prints no effective/clear diameters for any surface, same situation as p200/p300/p400/p500.
halfFieldDeg = 2.5175 is derived by halving the patent's own printed 2ω = 5.035° (not independently stated by the patent as a half-angle).

stated.totalLength = 424.803 mm is the patent's own printed TL (first surface to image plane at infinity focus); not used by the self-check (which reproduces f and Bf from the surface data) but recorded since it is patent-stated.

Patent JP2015-215560A (application JP2014-099625, filed 5/13/2014; published 12/3/2015; granted as JP6344044B2 on 6/20/2018) contains three numerical examples in one family: Example 1 (f=490.00, used here for the 500 mm f/4E FL slot), Example 2 (f=392.00, close to a 400 mm class), and Example 3 (f=588.00, close to a 600 mm class -- plausibly the sibling AF-S NIKKOR 600mm f/4E FL ED VR announced the same day, 7/2/2015, though that tie was not investigated here since it is out of scope for this task).
